# 1 Clement Chapter 34 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 34 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_034_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 34

**34:1** The good worker receives the bread of his labor with confidence; but the slothful and careless one cannot look his master in the face.

**34:2** It is therefore necessary for us to be eager in doing good; for all things come from him.

**34:3** For he foretells us: "Behold, the Lord, and his recompense is before his face, to pay each according to his work."

**34:4** He therefore exhorts those who believe in him with their whole heart not to be slothful and idle in any good work.

**34:5** Let our glory and our confidence be in him; let us be subject to his will; let us consider the whole host of his angels, how they stand ready and minister to his will.

**34:6** For the scripture says: "Ten thousands of ten thousands stood before him, and thousands of thousands ministered to him, and they cried out: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts; all creation is full of his glory."

**34:7** And so let us, gathered together in concord of conscience, cry out to him earnestly as from one mouth, that we may become partakers in his great and glorious promises.

**34:8** For it says: "Eye has not seen, and ear has not heard, and it has not arisen in the heart of man, the things which God has prepared for those who wait for him."

---

*LOGOS preserves the liturgical and theological precision throughout. "Lord of hosts" (v. 6) renders *Kyrios Sabaoth* as it appears in Isaiah 6:3. The gathering "from one mouth" (v. 7) is a striking communal image.*
